stem:
Zambezi Tennis Club in Harare keeps only a cash book. At 1 January 2025 its assets were the clubhouse US\$38,000, equipment US\$5,700, bar inventory US\$710, subscriptions in arrears US\$290, bank US\$3,260 and cash US\$95. Its liabilities were subscriptions received in advance US\$130, bar suppliers US\$430 and the groundsman's wages owing US\$205.

| Receipts for 2025 | US\$ | Payments for 2025 | US\$ |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| Subscriptions | 9,570 | Bar suppliers | 9,140 |
| Bar takings | 14,360 | Groundsman's wages | 4,330 |
| Entrance fees | 470 | Bar steward's wages | 2,640 |
| Donations (general) | 620 | Utilities | 1,790 |
| Competition entry fees | 1,230 | Prizes | 810 |
|  |  | New equipment | 1,460 |
|  |  | Administration | 970 |

At 31 December 2025: subscriptions in arrears US\$345 (after writing off US\$70 as irrecoverable) and in advance US\$170; bar suppliers owed US\$575; groundsman owed US\$255; bar inventory US\$730. Equipment is depreciated at 10% on cost including additions and the clubhouse at 2% of its value at the start of the year.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the accumulated fund at 1 January 2025.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate:

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: the subscriptions income for the year

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: the bar purchases for the year

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Bar trading account:

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: calculate the gross profit on the bar

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: calculate the profit on the bar after the bar steward's wages

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Prepare the income and expenditure account for the year ended 31 December 2025.

points.description: Heading with the name of the club and the period
Subscriptions 9,655 (own figure) and entrance fees
Competition entry fees 1,230 and donations 620
Profit on the bar 2,455 (own figure) and total income 14,430
Groundsman's wages 4,380
Irrecoverable subscriptions 70 as an expense
Depreciation 716 and 760; no charge for the equipment bought
Total expenditure 9,496 and surplus 4,934

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the accumulated fund at 31 December 2025.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Explain why the club's cash book summary (receipts and payments) is not enough to show the club's performance for the year.

points.description: It shows cash only and ignores accruals, prepayments and arrears
It includes capital payments such as equipment and does not show depreciation
It does not show a surplus or deficit or the assets and liabilities

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A cash summary shows cash only, so it ignores accruals, prepayments and arrears. It mixes capital items like new equipment with revenue items and has no depreciation, so it shows neither a surplus or deficit nor the assets and liabilities.

parts.explanation: One mark each for cash only, capital items and missing results.

explanation: This ZIMSEC Paper 2 style question combines the accumulated fund, subscriptions, the bar and the income and expenditure account of a club.
hints: Convert each cash figure using the opening and closing balances.
The write-off is on the credit side of the subscriptions account.
The equipment bought is not an expense.

stem:
Nyasha Furniture Works in Gweru makes wooden tables. The following information is for the year ended 31 October 2025.

| Item | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Raw materials: inventory at 1 November 2024 | 18,700 |
| Purchases of raw materials | 112,300 |
| Carriage inwards | 3,300 |
| Returns outwards (raw materials) | 2,900 |
| Raw materials: inventory at 31 October 2025 | 20,100 |
| Manufacturing wages | 74,100 |
| Royalties on tables made | 4,900 |
| Indirect factory wages | 16,100 |
| Work in progress at 1 November 2024 | 9,300 |
| Work in progress at 31 October 2025 | 10,600 |

Shared expenses for the year: rent and rates US\$23,600 (65% factory), power US\$12,900 (85% factory) and insurance US\$5,700 (55% factory). Machinery is depreciated at 12.5% on cost of US\$98,000; office equipment at 10% on cost of US\$17,000. The factory completed 3,000 tables.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the cost of raw materials consumed.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the prime cost.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the amount of each shared expense that is a factory overhead:

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: rent and rates

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: power

parts.label: (iii)
parts.stem: insurance

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the total factory overheads, including the depreciation of machinery.
parts.explanation: 16,100 + 15,340 + 10,965 + 3,135 + 12,250 = 57,790. Office equipment depreciation is not a factory cost.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 16,100 + 15,340 + 10,965 + 3,135 + 12,250 = 57,790. Office equipment depreciation is not a factory cost.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Prepare the manufacturing account for the year ended 31 October 2025.

points.description: Heading with the business name and period
Raw materials consumed 111,300, with carriage inwards and returns outwards in the right place
Direct wages and royalties; prime cost 190,300 (own figure)
Factory overheads listed: indirect wages and the four apportioned or depreciation items
Total factory overheads 57,790 and factory cost 248,090
Opening work in progress added
Closing work in progress deducted
Cost of production 246,790 with brackets for deductions

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Nyasha Furniture Works: manufacturing account for the year ended 31 October 2025**

| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Opening inventory of raw materials |  | 18,700 |
| Purchases of raw materials |  | 112,300 |
| Carriage inwards |  | 3,300 |
| Less returns outwards |  | (2,900) |
| Less closing inventory of raw materials |  | (20,100) |
| **Cost of raw materials consumed** |  | 111,300 |
| Direct labour (manufacturing wages) |  | 74,100 |
| Royalties |  | 4,900 |
| **Prime cost** |  | 190,300 |
| Factory overheads |  |  |
| Indirect factory wages | 16,100 |  |
| Rent and rates (factory share) | 15,340 |  |
| Power (factory share) | 10,965 |  |
| Insurance (factory share) | 3,135 |  |
| Depreciation of machinery | 12,250 |  |
| Total factory overheads |  | 57,790 |
| **Factory cost** |  | 248,090 |
| Add opening work in progress |  | 9,300 |

parts.explanation: Selling and administration costs, and office equipment depreciation, are excluded.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Calculate the cost of production per table, to the nearest cent.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: A supplier offers to supply the same tables for US\$78 each. Evaluate whether Nyasha Furniture Works should stop making them and advise the owner.

points.description: The supplier's price of 78 is lower than the full cost of 82.26 per table
Some overheads (rent, insurance, machinery depreciation) would continue if production stopped, so the real saving is smaller
Only avoidable costs (materials, wages, power) should be compared with the 78
Non-financial factors: quality, reliability of delivery, loss of skilled workers
Advice: do not stop on the full-cost comparison alone; compare avoidable costs and test the supplier's quality first

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The supplier's price of US\$78 is below the full cost of US\$82.26 per table, but rent, insurance and depreciation would continue if production stopped, so the saving is smaller. Only avoidable costs should be compared. Quality and reliability also matter, so the owner should not stop making tables until avoidable costs and the supplier's quality are checked.

parts.explanation: One mark for each point in a balanced judgement.

explanation: This ZIMSEC Paper 2 style question combines the manufacturing account, apportionment of shared expenses, cost per unit and a make-or-buy evaluation.
hints: Carriage inwards is added to the cost of materials.
Only the factory share of shared expenses is a factory overhead.
Add opening and deduct closing work in progress.
